words.paradigmCellCalloutBody: One slot in a word's inflection pattern — "I go" in the present, for instance. Each form card asks for exactly one of them, never the whole table. (Technical term: paradigm cell.)
words.reviewCaption: One stack of cards — meanings, and word forms once you are ready for them.
words.countsCaption: How many words from your starter pack you can recall the meaning of. We count dictionary forms, not inflected ones — and this is not a pile of work waiting for you.
words.countsDefinitionsSummary: What solid, shaky and new mean
words.lemmaCalloutBody: The form you would look up — run, not running; child, not children. Every card on this page is a word in that form. "Solid" means you would still know the meaning about a week from now. Inflected forms are counted separately, on Progress. (Technical term: lemma.)

words.fragileDescription: You have reviewed the meaning already. It is not solid yet.

progress.title: Where you stand
progress.intro: This page shows what has actually been measured. And it says plainly where nothing has been. A level you were never tested on is not a level — so there is none here yet.
progress.skillsCaption: Each skill, what we know about it, and what would make it measurable
progress.overallWithheld: There is no overall level yet. We take the second-lowest of the skills that count — and right now none of them count. Inventing a number is exactly what we will not do.
progress.signalsIntro: Your level will be built from these seven measurements. Each one has a value and a status. Only a skill can have a level — that is why none of these carry a letter and a number.
progress.signalsCaption: The seven measurements, and whether anything has been recorded for each
progress.stabilityValue: {days} days on average, over {taskCount, plural, one {# card} other {# cards}} you have reviewed
progress.vocabularyValue: {held} of {poolSize} starter-pack words are solid — not scaled up to the whole language
progress.formMasteryValue: {held} of {poolSize} starter-pack word forms are solid — counted separately from vocabulary
progress.formMasteryPartialParadigmNote: {count, plural, one {For # solid verb we do not know every form yet — how well you handle its forms is uncertain} other {For # solid verbs we do not know every form yet — how well you handle their forms is uncertain}}
progress.emptyState: You have not reviewed anything yet, so nothing below has a value. That is how it starts — not a failure.
progress.doseIntro: The hours below are the number nobody else quotes: guided learning hours, counted from zero. It is the total up to that level, not the cost of one step.
progress.doseCaption: Guided hours up to each level, and what 15 minutes a day covers
progress.doseHabit: 15 minutes a day, without missing one, is about {hours} hours a year.
progress.doseBorrowedUncalibrated: These figures are borrowed and not tuned to your language: {name}, estimates from English teaching. Treat them as a rough ballpark, not a measurement. A guided hour is also teaching with feedback, which app minutes only partly are. So the comparison flatters the app rather than the other way round.
progress.doseBorrowedCalibrated: These figures come from {name} and are tuned for {calibratedFor}. A guided hour is teaching with feedback, which app minutes only partly are.
progress.doseNoNumerator: There is no line here for your own hours, because the app does not count them. It only measures how long you spent on each card — time inside reviews and nothing else. But a third to a half of what we recommend happens away from the app. A total built from card time alone would be wrong by an unknown amount. Divided into the hours above, that error would look precise.
progress.gapBody: There is no estimate of your whole vocabulary yet, and so no CEFR level derived from one. That would need a frequency-ranked word list large enough — the starter pack has two thousand words. The table that maps vocabulary to a level is not tuned for this language pair either. We would rather name that than guess it.

methodMenu.title: Ways you can practise
methodMenu.intro: Sixty-odd ways people really learn languages. Three questions narrow the list: How long do you have? What do you want to practise? How much energy is there? Narrow further only if you want to.
methodMenu.timeLabel: How much time do you have?
methodMenu.timeScaleHint: Short steps at the start — drag right for longer, up to a day or endless
methodMenu.skillLabel: What do you want to train?
methodMenu.energyLabel: How much energy do you have?
methodMenu.refineHint: Only if the list is still too long — hands, voice, or whether you need your eyes.
methodMenu.nothingFits: Nothing fits that right now. Try more time, another skill, or fewer limits.
methodMenu.dailyIntro: Three real options without a long decision: an easy one, a well-evidenced one, and one for variety. The full list is below.
methodMenu.catalogueUnavailable: We could not load the method catalogue. Nothing is being kept from you below — there is nothing to show. What went wrong:

methodMenu.sessionNotBuilt: Once this method runs in the app, you start it here. Until then: read what it does, and try it away from the app.

methodMenu.standingRecorded: {held} of {poolSize} starter-pack words are solid. No per-skill levels yet — recalling meanings measures neither reading nor listening, speaking or writing.

sections.commitments: Things you keep up over time

evidence.A: Strong evidence (grade A) — replicated, and shown outside the lab too
evidence.B: Solid evidence (grade B) — well supported, but with limits
evidence.C: Thin evidence (grade C) — plausible and widespread, but little studied
evidence.D: Not researched (grade D) — our decision, not a finding

evidenceProse.A: Replicated, and shown outside the lab too
evidenceProse.C: Plausible and widespread, but little studied

intensity.1: can be done tired or distracted

audio-cards.name: Audio cards you can use without looking
audio-cards.summary: The same cards, spoken, with your eyes free
audio-cards.trains: holding on to words while your eyes are elsewhere
audio-cards.doesNotDo: It cannot grade itself honestly. Marking your own spoken answer while walking is the loosest grading in the app, and the schedule inherits that guesswork.

back-translation.name: Back-translation with comparison
back-translation.summary: Translate out, translate back, compare with the original
back-translation.trains: structure, and it makes avoidance visible
back-translation.doesNotDo: It grades you against one wording. A different wording that is perfectly good will show up as a mistake, and the comparison cannot tell the two apart.

background-listening.name: Leaving it on in the background
background-listening.summary: Leave it playing while you do something else
background-listening.doesNotDo: Honestly: barely anything. It is in the catalogue because learners ask about it, and the answer is that unattended sound produces almost no learning.

book-you-know.name: A book you already know in your own language
book-you-know.summary: A book you know by heart, in the new language
book-you-know.doesNotDo: It lets you understand the story without understanding the sentences. Prior knowledge fills the gaps, so comprehension overstates what you read.

build-a-sentence.name: Build a sentence with a target word
build-a-sentence.summary: Write one sentence that uses a given word
build-a-sentence.trains: putting a word to use yourself
build-a-sentence.doesNotDo: Each sentence stands on its own. Nothing in it exercises holding a thought across several sentences, which is where most learners actually break down — and the check finds spelling and agreement, not word order, word choice or idiom.

caption-your-photos.name: Captioning your own photos
caption-your-photos.summary: Write a line under a photo of your own
caption-your-photos.trains: vocabulary you have a connection to
caption-your-photos.doesNotDo: It cannot be aimed. What your photos happen to contain decides the vocabulary, and that is unlikely to be what you most need.

close-a-frequency-block.name: Finishing off a group of common words
close-a-frequency-block.summary: Work all the way through one group of the frequency list
close-a-frequency-block.trains: how much of a text you understand
close-a-frequency-block.doesNotDo: It chases the number rather than the need. Finishing a group is satisfying, and it can spend a week on words you would never have missed.

cloze-sentences.name: Cloze sentences
cloze-sentences.summary: One word removed from a sentence; put it back
cloze-sentences.doesNotDo: The sentence around the gap does much of the work. A cloze you can solve from context alone measures the context, not the form.

collocation-cards.name: Word pairs rather than single words (collocations)
collocation-cards.summary: Learn a word together with the words it usually travels with
collocation-cards.trains: fluency — the word together with what belongs to it
collocation-cards.doesNotDo: It counts as one item what is really several. A word-pair card grows your vocabulary more slowly than the same minutes on single words.

cook-from-a-recipe.name: Cooking from a recipe in the language
cook-from-a-recipe.summary: Cook something, following the recipe in the language
cook-from-a-recipe.doesNotDo: It teaches the vocabulary of one kitchen. The consequences make you read carefully; they do not make the words general.

copy-a-paragraph.name: Copying out a good paragraph
copy-a-paragraph.summary: Copy out a well-written paragraph by hand
copy-a-paragraph.doesNotDo: It involves no choice at all. Every word is given, so it is handwriting and attention practice, not language production.

describe-a-picture.name: Describing a picture
describe-a-picture.summary: Say everything you can see in one photo
describe-a-picture.doesNotDo: It stays in the present tense and the third person. Pictures rarely require you to narrate, hypothesise or argue.

diary-three-sentences.name: Diary, three sentences
diary-three-sentences.doesNotDo: It circles the same life. Your days repeat, so the vocabulary it demands narrows rather than widens over months.

dictogloss.name: Listen, then rebuild it from memory (dictogloss)
dictogloss.summary: Listen twice, then rebuild the passage from memory
dictogloss.doesNotDo: It does not check that you heard the words. A good rebuild can come from the gist plus grammar, which is both the point and the limit.

extensive-reading.name: Reading a lot, without stopping
extensive-reading.summary: Read something you mostly understand, without stopping
extensive-reading.doesNotDo: It does not fix a word in memory. Words met while reading are met once; without the schedule picking them up they are gone in a week.

film-you-know-by-heart.name: Watching a film you know by heart
film-you-know-by-heart.summary: A film you know every line of, in the language
film-you-know-by-heart.doesNotDo: You already know what is being said. Memory does the comprehension, which is what makes it comfortable and what limits it.

four-three-two.summary: The same story in four minutes, then three, then two
four-three-two.doesNotDo: It improves nothing about accuracy. Telling the same thing three times faster makes delivery smoother and leaves the errors intact.

free-production.name: Writing freely
free-production.summary: Write freely on a prompt, with nothing to copy from
free-production.trains: writing under your own steam — and what you steer around
free-production.doesNotDo: It cannot make you use what you are dodging. Steering around a word is what it reveals, not what it repairs.

full-dictation.name: Full dictation on paper
full-dictation.summary: Hear a sentence, write the whole of it down
full-dictation.doesNotDo: It is slow and it does not teach meaning. Ten minutes buys six sentences of sound-to-spelling, and comprehension is not what is being checked.

handwriting-shakiest.name: Handwriting sheet of the twenty shakiest cards
handwriting-shakiest.summary: Write out the twenty cards you keep failing
handwriting-shakiest.doesNotDo: It is slow and it is off-app, so its result has to be typed back in or it produces no signal at all.

hobby-in-target-language.name: Pursue one hobby in the target language
hobby-in-target-language.summary: One thing you love, done in the language
hobby-in-target-language.doesNotDo: It builds one subject deeply. Someone who can discuss climbing gear fluently may still be unable to describe their week.

intensive-reading.name: Reading closely, word by word
intensive-reading.summary: One paragraph, taken apart until nothing is unclear
intensive-reading.doesNotDo: It builds no quantity. One paragraph gone over exhaustively is the opposite of the reading volume fluency needs, and it cannot stand in for it.

interpreting.name: Interpreting for someone
interpreting.summary: Carry what one person says across to another
interpreting.doesNotDo: It overwhelms before it teaches. Unless you already handle both directions reasonably well, it produces failure rather than practice.

label-the-flat.name: Label the flat
label-the-flat.summary: Names on the things you walk past every day
label-the-flat.doesNotDo: Labels teach nouns on their own, which is the one thing cards already do well. You stop seeing them after a week.

listening-faster.name: Listening faster (1.25×)
listening-faster.summary: Something you already follow, a quarter faster
listening-faster.doesNotDo: It adds no vocabulary. Speeding up material you already understand rehearses the following-along you have, not the words you lack.

listening-level-1.name: Listening only, with no text
listening-level-1.summary: Listen once, with no text to fall back on
listening-level-1.doesNotDo: It gives no partial credit. With no text in front of you, you cannot see which word you missed — only that you missed one.

mine-your-own-sentences.name: Collecting sentences from your own reading
mine-your-own-sentences.summary: Turn sentences from what you read into cards
mine-your-own-sentences.doesNotDo: It ignores how common a word is. Words you happen to meet are not the words that unlock the most text, and collecting alone leaves common ones unlearned for years.

minimal-pairs.name: Telling similar sounds apart (minimal pairs)
minimal-pairs.summary: Two words that differ by one sound — which was it?
minimal-pairs.doesNotDo: Hearing a difference is not saying it. Training your ear carries over to your mouth only partly, and it trains sounds rather than words.

narrow-listening.name: One series, one speaker
narrow-listening.summary: One series, one voice, until the voice is easy
narrow-listening.doesNotDo: It tunes you to one voice. Getting comfortable with one speaker's rate and accent transfers to other speakers far less than it feels like it should.

narrow-reading.name: Several texts on the same subject
narrow-reading.summary: Four texts on one subject, so the words come back
narrow-reading.trains: the same as reading a lot, faster — one subject's words keep coming back
narrow-reading.doesNotDo: It broadens nothing. Four texts on one subject build that subject's vocabulary and leave the rest of the language exactly where it was.

one-series-target-audio.name: Watch one series only with target-language audio
one-series-target-audio.summary: One series you never watch in your own language
one-series-target-audio.doesNotDo: It relies on subtitles going off eventually. With them on, most of the hours go to reading.

order-ask-complain.name: Ordering, asking, complaining
order-ask-complain.summary: Do a real errand in the language, out loud
order-ask-complain.doesNotDo: It is a handful of fixed exchanges. Once they work you can repeat them for years without adding anything.

own-error-log.name: Working through your own list of mistakes
own-error-log.summary: Work through the mistakes you actually made
own-error-log.trains: your own patterns rather than the average learner's
own-error-log.doesNotDo: It only contains errors you were caught making. Everything you avoid saying never reaches the log.

paradigm-tables-mixed.name: Form tables, mixed up
paradigm-tables-mixed.summary: Fill in forms from different patterns, not one table at a time
paradigm-tables-mixed.trains: hitting the right form without thinking
paradigm-tables-mixed.doesNotDo: It does not carry into speech on its own. Filling a slot in a table on demand is a long way from producing it mid-sentence.

parallel-text.name: Parallel text
parallel-text.summary: The same passage in both languages, side by side
parallel-text.doesNotDo: It removes the retrieval attempt. With the translation beside it, nothing forces you to work the meaning out, and unworked meaning does not stick.

partial-dictation.name: Partial dictation
partial-dictation.summary: Hear a sentence, fill in the words that were taken out
partial-dictation.trains: hearing the sounds, recalling them by ear
partial-dictation.doesNotDo: It measures the gaps and nothing else. The words you were handed tell you nothing about whether you would have heard them.

reading-aloud.name: Reading aloud
reading-aloud.summary: Read a passage out loud, at a speaking pace
reading-aloud.trains: pronunciation, flow, hearing where words begin and end
reading-aloud.doesNotDo: It is not speaking. Every word is chosen for you, so it trains how you form sounds and hold a rhythm while leaving recall untouched.

reading-while-listening.name: Reading and listening at once
reading-while-listening.summary: Follow the text while a voice reads it to you
reading-while-listening.trains: listening, hearing where words begin and end
reading-while-listening.doesNotDo: It does not test listening. The text carries you, so it cannot tell you what you would have understood without it.

recite-memorised.name: Reciting a memorised poem or monologue
recite-memorised.summary: Say a piece you have learned by heart
recite-memorised.trains: the melody of the language, set phrases
recite-memorised.doesNotDo: It is recall of one fixed string. Nothing in it generalises to a sentence you have not memorised.

repeated-listening.name: Repeated listening with support removal
repeated-listening.summary: The same clip three times, with less help each pass
repeated-listening.doesNotDo: It does not build quantity, and by the third pass you are recalling the clip rather than working it out.

reread-something-hard.name: Re-read something that was too hard
reread-something-hard.summary: Open something that beat you months ago
reread-something-hard.trains: the feeling of having got somewhere
reread-something-hard.doesNotDo: It teaches almost nothing new. Its whole value is evidence of progress you can feel, which is a motivation effect and not a learning one.

retell-what-you-read.name: Retelling what you just read
retell-what-you-read.summary: Close the text and say what it said
retell-what-you-read.trains: saying it yourself — from understanding to speaking
retell-what-you-read.doesNotDo: It borrows the source's vocabulary. What comes out is partly the text's phrasing echoed back, so it overstates what you can say unprompted.

rewrite-in-your-own-words.name: Rewriting a text in your own words
rewrite-in-your-own-words.summary: Say the same thing again, differently
rewrite-in-your-own-words.doesNotDo: It rewards saying it another way over saying it precisely, and someone short of vocabulary will reformulate downwards into what they already have.

role-play.name: Role play or drama
role-play.summary: Act out a situation with someone else
role-play.doesNotDo: It needs other people, so it cannot be the thing you fall back on. A method that requires company is unavailable most of the time by construction.

rule-at-point-of-error.name: Rule explanation at the point of error
rule-at-point-of-error.summary: Read why that was wrong, the moment it goes wrong
rule-at-point-of-error.trains: understanding, exactly when it is wanted
rule-at-point-of-error.doesNotDo: Understanding a rule is not being able to apply it. It removes confusion; it does not produce automaticity.

self-talk.name: Self-talk — describe what you see
self-talk.summary: Describe what is in front of you, out loud
self-talk.doesNotDo: Nobody corrects you. Errors repeated aloud in private get rehearsed as readily as correct forms do.

sentence-transformation.name: Rebuilding sentences — tense, negation, person
sentence-transformation.summary: Take a sentence and change its tense or its person
sentence-transformation.trains: flexibility with forms you already meet
sentence-transformation.doesNotDo: It supplies the sentence. You never have to decide what to say, only how to bend it.

shadowing.name: Speaking along, a beat behind (shadowing)
shadowing.summary: Repeat a voice a beat behind it, without stopping
shadowing.trains: the melody of the language, flow
shadowing.doesNotDo: It never asks you to choose a word. Following a voice at a delay trains how you form sounds, not recall, and it works with very little understanding.

shopping-list-in-your-head.name: Think through your shopping list in the target language
shopping-list-in-your-head.summary: Run everyday lists through the language in your head
shopping-list-in-your-head.trains: recalling words in the middle of ordinary life
shopping-list-in-your-head.doesNotDo: You will notice the words you lack and then move on without looking them up, so the gap gets found and not filled.

singing-along.name: Singing along
singing-along.summary: Sing with the recording, words in front of you
singing-along.trains: the melody of the language, set phrases
singing-along.doesNotDo: Song rhythm overrides speech rhythm. Stress and vowel length get bent to the melody, so the prosody you practise is not the prosody you need.

srs-session.name: Reviewing at growing intervals
srs-session.summary: The cards the schedule says are due today
srs-session.doesNotDo: It builds nothing you can use in a sentence. Cards make words come back on their own, and the rest of the app exists because that is not the same as knowing them.

summarise-what-you-read.name: Summarising what you read
summarise-what-you-read.summary: Say what a text said, shorter, in writing
summarise-what-you-read.doesNotDo: It lets you lift phrases straight out. Without a deliberate pause between reading and writing, much of what appears is copied rather than your own.

switch-phone-language.name: Switch your phone's language
switch-phone-language.summary: Your phone speaks the language from now on
switch-phone-language.doesNotDo: It teaches interface words and stops. Within a fortnight you stop reading the menus at all and it becomes invisible.

tandem-or-language-cafe.name: Tandem or language café
tandem-or-language-cafe.summary: Talk to a speaker who is also learning yours
tandem-or-language-cafe.doesNotDo: Half of it is in your own language, and a patient partner will accommodate you until neither of you notices what you cannot say.

translate-a-song.name: Translating a song
translate-a-song.summary: Work out what a song you like actually says
translate-a-song.doesNotDo: Lyrics are unrepresentative. Inverted word order and archaic vocabulary are normal in songs and wrong in speech.

video-game-in-target-language.name: A video game in the target language
video-game-in-target-language.summary: Play something with the language switched over
video-game-in-target-language.doesNotDo: Games are playable without reading. Once you know the interface you stop parsing the text, and the practice quietly ends while the play continues.

voice-message.name: A voice message to a real person
voice-message.summary: Send one spoken message to somebody real
voice-message.doesNotDo: It cannot be scheduled around your weak forms. You will say what you needed to say, which is the value and also why it trains nothing in particular.

write-and-perform-a-play.name: Writing and performing a play
write-and-perform-a-play.summary: Write something short and put it on
write-and-perform-a-play.doesNotDo: It runs for weeks and produces one measurement. As a project it is excellent; as something to measure you by, nearly useless.

write-to-one-friend.name: Write to one friend only in the target language
write-to-one-friend.summary: One person you only ever write to in the language
write-to-one-friend.trains: writing when you really want to be understood
write-to-one-friend.doesNotDo: Nobody corrects you and nothing is recorded. It is the highest-leverage entry in the catalogue and the app cannot see a single thing about it.

install.title: Add to Home Screen
install.intro: On iPhone, the Home Screen app only works properly if you add it from the main site — not from Methods, Words or Progress.
install.whyBody: Apple remembers the page you were on when you tapped Add to Home Screen. Added from the main site, every section works without Safari's bottom bar. Added from a section page, only that one section stays clean.
install.noButton: iPhone allows websites no install button. You do it through Safari's Share menu → Add to Home Screen.
steps: Remove any existing Home Screen icon for this app.
Open the main website in Safari (button below — not a bookmark to Methods or Words).
Tap Share (square with arrow) → Add to Home Screen → Add.
Open the app only from the new icon. Sign in if prompted.
install.openSiteAria: Open the main website to add this app to your Home Screen
install.alreadySignedIn: If you are signed in here in the browser, you can still add to Home Screen from this page — the Home Screen app will ask you to sign in again.

landing.eyebrow: Language learning with methods that are backed up
landing.headline: You choose how you practise — we show whether you're really getting somewhere.
landing.subhead: Sixty-plus well-evidenced ways to practise. You take what fits today — we show you what it does for you.
landing.timeHonesty: 15 minutes a day, without missing one, is about {hours} hours a year. From a standing start that is roughly a quarter of the way to B1. If that feels slow, it is the arithmetic, not you.

pillars.text: We show you what you can actually do — not how busy you were.
